Codes of practice – Code D Identification of persons by police officers
31

6 Identification by body samples and impressions
(A) General

6.1 References to:
(a) an ‘intimate sample’ mean a dental impression or sample of blood, semen or any other
tissue fluid, urine, or pubic hair, or a swab taken from any part of a person’s genitals
or from a person's body orifice other than the mouth;
(b) a ‘non-intimate sample’ means:
(i) a sample of hair, other than pubic hair, which includes hair plucked with the root,
see Note 6A;
(ii) a sample taken from a nail or from under a nail;
(iii) a swab taken from any part of a person’s body other than a part from which a
swab taken would be an intimate sample;
(iv) saliva;
(v) a skin impression which means any record, other than a fingerprint, which is a
record, in any form and produced by any method, of the skin pattern and other
physical characteristics or features of the whole, or any part of, a person’s foot or
of any other part of their body.
